item.text:
I used the local prior as the factual floor and did not re-fetch structured country-year datasets already present there. I only looked for narrative and attribution sources that help explain Xi Jinping’s 2022 office, constraints, and key events.

**Office and constraints**
- In 2022 Xi held four top posts: CPC general secretary, CPC Central Military Commission chair, PRC president, and PRC Central Military Commission chair.
- His authority was primarily party-centered, not competitive-electoral. The PRC constitution defines the formal state powers of the presidency, while the CPC constitution and 20th Party Congress texts anchor authority in the Party and in Xi’s “core” position.
- The main constraints in 2022 were intra-party discipline, policy performance, and elite-management pressure, especially around zero-COVID, the economy, and succession optics.

**Retained sources**
1. [Brief introduction of Xi Jinping](https://english.www.gov.cn/english.www.gov.cn/Homepage/202210/24/content_WS641af593c6d0f528699db898.html) - State Council / Xinhua, 2022-10-24. Fact: Xi was listed as general secretary, CMC chair, president, and PRC CMC chair. Fit: exact 2022 office snapshot. Attribution: explicit, ruler-specific. Limits: official profile; no dissent or implementation detail. Contrary points: does not show how much actual discretion was constrained by Party bodies.

2. [Constitution of the People’s Republic of China](https://www.npc.gov.cn/englishnpc/constitution2019/201911/t20191120_384295.html) - NPC, 2019-11-20 consolidated text. Fact: the NPC elects the president; the constitution defines formal presidential powers and term structure. Fit: legal baseline during 2022. Attribution: state-level, not personal. Limits: describes law on paper, not how Party power works. Contrary points: Party supremacy and Xi’s “core” status sit above this formal text in practice.

3. [中国共产党章程](https://www.xinhuanet.com/2022-10/26/c_1129081750.htm) - Xinhua, 2022-10-26. Fact: the amended CPC Constitution embeds Xi’s core position and the guiding role of Xi Thought. Fit: post-congress institutionalization of power. Attribution: direct party attribution. Limits: propagandistic and self-justifying. Contrary points: does not capture any internal dissent.

4. [（二十大受权发布）中国共产党第二十次全国代表大会在京闭幕 习近平主持大会并发表重要讲话](https://www.xinhuanet.com/politics/leaders/2022-10/22/c_1129075392.htm) - Xinhua, 2022-10-22. Fact: the congress elected a new central committee and CCDI and passed the party-constitution amendment. Fit: the key 2022 power-consolidation event. Attribution: direct, explicit. Limits: official event framing. Contrary points: omits the Hu Jintao removal and any backstage contention.

5. [习近平：高举中国特色社会主义伟大旗帜 为全面建设社会主义现代化国家而团结奋斗](https://www.xinhuanet.com/politics/leaders/2022-10/25/c_1129079429.htm) - Xinhua, 2022-10-25. Fact: Xi’s congress report set the strategic frame around modernization, security, and national rejuvenation. Fit: the 2022–2027 policy blueprint. Attribution: Xi as author/speaker. Limits: programmatic, not evidence of implementation. Contrary points: later 2022 events showed sharp policy stress and reversal.

6. [Chinese ex-President Hu Jintao escorted out of party congress](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/chinese-ex-president-hu-jintao-escorted-out-of-party-congress-2918972) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-10-22. Fact: Hu Jintao was unexpectedly escorted out during the closing session. Fit: elite-control signal at the congress. Attribution: indirect, via Xi’s presence and the congress setting. Limits: Reuters witness reporting plus official silence; cause remained disputed. Contrary points: official explanation said he was unwell.

7. [China’s zero-COVID policy dashes global hopes for quick economic return to normal](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/chinas-zerocovid-policy-dashes-global-hopes-for-quick-economic-return-to-normal-2827802) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-05-19. Fact: strict zero-COVID rules were still dragging on growth and global trade. Fit: inherited policy constraint for 2022. Attribution: regime/policy attribution, not personal causation alone. Limits: analytical reporting, not official data. Contrary points: official sources continued to frame the policy as necessary and scientific.

8. [上海连夜辟谣“封城”传言 对部分区域封控开展全员筛查](https://m.caixin.com/m/2022-03-23/101859763.html) - 财新网, 2022-03-23. Fact: Shanghai was under partial containment and broad screening, with the city resisting the “citywide lockdown” label. Fit: spring 2022 lockdown shock and local implementation strain. Attribution: local party-state policy under Xi-era zero-COVID. Limits: access-limited; city-level, not national attribution. Contrary points: official framing minimized the breadth of the shutdown.

9. [China property market slumps on developers’ debt crisis, weak buyer sentiment](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/china-property-market-slumps-on-developers-debt-crisis-weak-buyer-sentiment-2830349) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-05-26. Fact: the property sector was weakened by debt stress, lockdowns, and weak demand. Fit: major inherited economic drag in 2022. Attribution: national policy context, not Xi personal action alone. Limits: market-focused and macro-level. Contrary points: later easing did not immediately fix the slump.

10. [Blank sheets of paper become symbol of defiance in China protests](https://www.investing.com/news/coronavirus/blank-sheets-of-paper-become-symbol-of-defiance-in-china-protests-2952307) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-11-27. Fact: protests spread across multiple cities against COVID curbs, with unusually direct anti-Xi sentiment in some places. Fit: late-2022 mass-discontent peak. Attribution: indirect but clearly tied to Xi’s signature policy. Limits: censorship and witness-based verification gaps. Contrary points: official media and censors downplayed the scope and political meaning.

11. [关于进一步优化落实新冠肺炎疫情防控措施的通知](https://www.nhc.gov.cn/xcs/gzzcwj/202212/15457b5897ba42c991e3ee3b1f1f4bed.shtml) - National Health Commission / joint prevention mechanism, 2022-12-07. Fact: China announced 10 optimization measures, including narrower lockdown rules and reduced testing. Fit: policy pivot after protest pressure. Attribution: state-policy shift, not personal applause. Limits: implementation varied widely by locality. Contrary points: looks reactive rather than a planned smooth transition.

12. [China holds Central Economic Work Conference to plan for 2023](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/topnews/202212/17/content_WS639d0051c6d0a757729e4885.html) - State Council / Xinhua, 2022-12-17. Fact: Xi reviewed 2022 economic work and set 2023 priorities around stability and demand expansion. Fit: year-end reset after a difficult year. Attribution: explicit Xi leadership. Limits: official summary; optimistic framing. Contrary points: Reuters/Caixin reporting shows the underlying economy was weaker than the tone suggested.

**Compact event map**
- March to May: Shanghai lockdown dynamics exposed the cost of zero-COVID.
- May to July: zero-COVID still dominated policy; property stress and weak growth deepened.
- October 16 to 23: 20th Party Congress, Xi report, congress closure, Party Constitution revision, Xi reaffirmed as core leader.
- October 22: Hu Jintao’s removal from the closing session became a major elite-politics signal.
- Late November: protests spread across China against COVID restrictions.
- December 7 to 8: official optimization of COVID controls began.
- December 15 to 16: Central Economic Work Conference reset the 2023 economic line toward stability and recovery.

**Chapter source plan**
- 1B: not enough ruler-conduct evidence in this pass; if needed later, use FAS, NTI, SIPRI, and official defense white papers.
- 2B: use official congress texts plus Reuters on elite management; local structured UCDP/SIPRI facts already cover the baseline.
- 3B: use Caixin Shanghai, Reuters protest coverage, and NHC COVID notices; local CIRIGHTS/PTS/V-Dem facts already provide the baseline repression metrics.
- 4B: use the PRC Constitution, Xi profile, CPC Constitution amendment, and congress closure/report texts.
- 5B: use Reuters on property stress and zero-COVID drag, plus the Central Economic Work Conference and Caixin macro commentary.
- 6B: use official health-policy shifts and the local welfare structured facts; little extra narrative sourcing is needed.
- 7B: use Party Constitution / congress materials plus Reuters on Hu Jintao and the broader discipline-control environment.
- 8B: use the Central Economic Work Conference, Xi’s congress report, and Reuters/Caixin economy coverage for governance-capacity context.
